title: Tree Codec
statement:
Turn a binary tree into text and rebuild an identical tree from that text.

Contract
- Implement `serialize`, which converts a tree (possibly null) into a non-null string, and `deserialize`, which converts a string produced by `serialize` back into a tree.
- For every tree, `deserialize(serialize(root))` must be a new tree with exactly the same shape and node values. Values may be any `int`, including negative ones and zero; missing children must be preserved.
- You choose the text format. Tests only check that the round trip rebuilds the tree, not what the string looks like. Keep no state between calls.
- Trees may be lopsided, with a height of up to 1000 nodes.

Examples
- The round trip of `[1, 2, 3, null, null, 4, 5]` is `[1, 2, 3, null, null, 4, 5]`.
- The round trip of a null tree is a null tree.
- The round trip of `[-1, -2, null, -3]` is `[-1, -2, null, -3]`.
hints: A list of values alone cannot tell where children are missing, so the text needs an explicit marker for an absent child.

Write the tree in a fixed traversal order, using a marker for each null child and a separator between tokens. To rebuild, read tokens in the same order with a shared position index, creating a node for each value and recursing for its children.
Each node is written and read once. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for n nodes, so build the string with a StringBuilder rather than repeated concatenation.
inputSyntax: Input: the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: [1, 2, 3, null, null, 4, 5]
